title: Dual-modal Depth Sensitive Magnetic Imaging of 3D Skyrmions in Multilayer Thin Films
content: Magnetic skyrmions are whorls of magnetic spins with a complex structure linked to a non-trivial topological charge. This topology gives rise to several useful properties, such as energetic stability and efficient transport, making skyrmions promising candidates for logical bits in spintronics and storage devices [1-3]. While the skyrmion as a theoretical construct is defined in two spatial dimensions, recent studies have spurred interest in the magnetic skyrmion’s structure in three spatial dimensions. Multilayer thin films which lack the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI) are of particular interest. These samples host dipole-stabilized skyrmions which are expected to feature a depth varying structure consisting of a Bloch-like core with Néel-like closure domains at the sample surfaces [4-8]. This “hybrid skyrmion” structure can be understood as a twisting of the domain wall helicity from core to surface.
